q: Wave motion is a method of transferring energy by successive _____ through the medium.
e: Wave motion is a method of transferring energy by successive disturbances through the medium. Disturbances here means the travelling pulses that carry wave energy through a medium. Particles: bits of the medium; the wave can pass energy without carrying them away.

q: In wave motion, the movement of energy takes place without transferring _____.
e: In wave motion, the movement of energy takes place without transferring matter. Matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space. Energy: the capacity to do work.

q: All waves are produced by a _____ source.
e: All waves are produced by a vibrating source. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating.

q: Energy and _____ are transferred through the medium from the wave source.
e: Energy and momentum are transferred through the medium from the wave source. Momentum here means mass times velocity, so it is directed. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Mechanical waves need a material medium to propagate and cannot pass through _____.
e: Mechanical waves need a material medium to propagate and cannot pass through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: Sound waves and seismic waves are examples of _____ waves.
e: Sound waves and seismic waves are examples of mechanical waves. The physics in this sentence is built around mechanical.

q: Electromagnetic waves can pass through vacuum and they do not need _____ for propagation.
e: Electromagnetic waves can pass through vacuum and they do not need medium for propagation. The physics in this sentence is built around medium. Energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Light waves and X-rays are examples of _____ waves.
e: Light waves and X-rays are examples of electromagnetic waves. The physics in this sentence is built around electromagnetic.

q: When a stone is dropped onto a quiet surface of a pond, the water in the pond does not move from the centre to the _____.
e: When a stone is dropped onto a quiet surface of a pond, the water in the pond does not move from the centre to the edges. The physics in this sentence is built around edges.

q: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on the _____ of particles in the medium.
e: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on the vibration of particles in the medium. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound. Speed: how fast the path length changes, with no direction.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a _____ wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave. Transverse names if the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave.

q: Waves in a vibrating string are examples of _____ waves.
e: Waves in a vibrating string are examples of transverse waves. The physics in this sentence is built around transverse.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a _____ wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of the medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave. Longitudinal names if the displacements of particles of the medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave.

q: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are _____ waves.
e: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are longitudinal waves. The physics in this sentence is built around longitudinal.

q: A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a _____ coiled spring.
e: A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a slinky coiled spring. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound.

q: Water waves are a good example of _____ waves.
e: Water waves are a good example of combinational waves. The physics in this sentence is built around combinational.

q: The highest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The highest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave crest. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The lowest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The lowest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave trough. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests or two consecutive wave troughs is called _____.
e: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests or two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength. Wavelength here means the distance from one crest to the next crest. Amplitude: the maximum displacement of the vibrating particle.

q: The SI unit of wavelength is the _____.
e: The SI unit of wavelength is the metre. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: Generally, the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of the same _____.
e: Generally, the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of the same phase. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda. Amplitude: the maximum displacement of the vibrating particle.

q: The number of complete waves passing a point per second is called the _____ of the wave.
e: The number of complete waves passing a point per second is called the frequency of the wave. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Period: the time for one complete vibration.

q: The SI unit of frequency is the _____.
e: The SI unit of frequency is the hertz. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: One hertz is equal to one complete _____ per second.
e: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. The physics in this sentence is built around cycle. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests is called the _____ of a wave.
e: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests is called the period of a wave. Period here means the time for one complete vibration. Frequency: how many complete waves pass a point each second.

q: The unit of period is the _____.
e: The unit of period is the second. The unit that belongs with this quantity is second.

q: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the _____.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The mathematical relationship between period $T$ and frequency $f$ is _____.
e: The mathematical relationship between period $T$ and frequency $f$ is $T = \frac{1}{f}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The amplitude of a wave is the _____ value of displacement of a vibrating particle.
e: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of a vibrating particle. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The velocity of a wave is the _____ with which a wave crest travels.
e: The velocity of a wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: The unit of wave velocity is _____.
e: The unit of wave velocity is $\text{m s}^{-1}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called _____ waves.
e: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called sine waves. Sine names most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called waves.

q: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is given by the equation _____.
e: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is given by the equation $v = f \lambda$. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a particular instant of _____.
e: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a particular instant of time. Time here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force.

q: In a displacement-distance graph, the displacement of the particle is plotted on the _____.
e: In a displacement-distance graph, the displacement of the particle is plotted on the y-axis. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of a particle of a certain position as a function of _____ taken to travel by a wave.
e: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of a particle of a certain position as a function of time taken to travel by a wave. Time here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Distance: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: In a displacement-time graph, the time interval is plotted on the _____.
e: In a displacement-time graph, the time interval is plotted on the x-axis. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of _____.
e: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of waves. The physics in this sentence is built around waves.

q: The surface that joins all the points of the same phase is called a _____.
e: The surface that joins all the points of the same phase is called a wavefront. Wavefront names the surface that joins all the points of the same phase. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The turning back of waves when they strike an obstacle is called the _____ of waves.
e: The turning back of waves when they strike an obstacle is called the reflection of waves. Reflection here means light bouncing back from a surface. Refraction: light bending as it changes medium.

q: When waves strike a straight barrier, the angle of incidence is _____ to the angle of reflection.
e: When waves strike a straight barrier, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. The physics in this sentence is built around equal.

q: In the reflection of waves, the wavelength and velocity of the wave remain _____.
e: In the reflection of waves, the wavelength and velocity of the wave remain constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: When plane waves strike a concave barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When plane waves strike a concave barrier, the reflected waves converge. The physics in this sentence is built around converge.

q: When plane waves strike a convex barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When plane waves strike a convex barrier, the reflected waves diverge. The physics in this sentence is built around diverge.

q: The speed of water waves depends on the _____ of water.
e: The speed of water waves depends on the depth of water. The physics in this sentence is built around depth. Temperature: how hot or cold a body is.

q: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water, the velocity of the wave is _____ and the wavelength is shorter.
e: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water, the velocity of the wave is lesser and the wavelength is shorter. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: A change in direction of waves when they are incident to the boundary with an angle is called _____.
e: A change in direction of waves when they are incident to the boundary with an angle is called refraction. Refraction here means light bending as it changes medium. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: In refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but the _____ remains the same.
e: In refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but the frequency remains the same. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Speed: how fast the path length changes, with no direction.

q: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap or around an _____.
e: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap or around an obstacle. The physics in this sentence is built around obstacle.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the wider the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In the diffraction of water waves, the wider the gap, the less the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around less.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the narrower the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In the diffraction of water waves, the narrower the gap, the more the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around more.

q: In diffraction, the wavelength of the wave does not _____.
e: In diffraction, the wavelength of the wave does not change. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: Sound is a form of _____ that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.
e: Sound is a form of energy that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium. Energy here means the capacity to do work. Matter: anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: Sound wave is produced by a _____ object placed in a medium.
e: Sound wave is produced by a vibrating object placed in a medium. The physics in this sentence is built around vibrating.

q: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and _____ like longitudinal waves.
e: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and rarefaction like longitudinal waves. In a longitudinal wave the particles shake along the travel, as in sound. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate and cannot travel through _____.
e: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate and cannot travel through vacuum. Vacuum here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube.

q: The compression region in a sound wave has _____ pressure.
e: The compression region in a sound wave has higher pressure. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When the vibrating object moves back, the molecules are spread out and _____ is created.
e: When the vibrating object moves back, the molecules are spread out and rarefaction is created. The physics in this sentence is built around rarefaction.

q: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by successive pressure changes without moving the _____ as a whole.
e: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by successive pressure changes without moving the medium as a whole. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure.

q: When sound waves enter the ear, they strike the _____ and make it vibrate.
e: When sound waves enter the ear, they strike the ear drum and make it vibrate. The physics in this sentence is built around ear drum.

q: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than _____ Hz.
e: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than 20 000 Hz. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The interval of frequency from 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz is called the _____ range.
e: The interval of frequency from 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz is called the audible range. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called _____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called ultrasounds. Ultrasounds names sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz.

q: Sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz are called _____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz are called infrasound. Infrasound names sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz.

q: Elephants can communicate with _____.
e: Elephants can communicate with infrasound. The physics in this sentence is built around infrasound.

q: Dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear and communicate with _____.
e: Dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear and communicate with ultrasound. The physics in this sentence is built around ultrasound.

q: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the _____ of the medium.
e: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the density of the medium. Density here means mass per unit volume.

q: The denser the medium is, the _____ the speed of sound because the particles are tightly bound together.
e: The denser the medium is, the greater the speed of sound because the particles are tightly bound together. The physics in this sentence is built around greater.

q: At 0°C, the speed of sound in air is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: At 0°C, the speed of sound in air is 332 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 332.

q: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, the speed of sound will increase by _____ %.
e: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, the speed of sound will increase by 0.2 %. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with a temperature rise of one degree.
e: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by 0.6 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with a temperature rise of one degree. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The speed of sound in air can be expressed by the formula $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$, where $T$ is given in _____.
e: The speed of sound in air can be expressed by the formula $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$, where $T$ is given in K. The physics in this sentence is built around K.

q: The approximate relation for the speed of sound in air with temperature $T$ in Kelvin is $v = $ _____.
e: The approximate relation for the speed of sound in air with temperature $T$ in Kelvin is $v = $ $332 + 0.6(T - 273)$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C is 1404 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 1404.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in copper at 20°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in copper at 20°C is 3560 $\text{m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around 3560.
